name: Chilli
soilType: Well-drained sandy loam or black loam with pH 6.5 - 7.5
growthTips: Avoid waterlogging at all stages; chilli roots rot quickly in waterlogged soil.
Spray Boron 20% @ 1g/L at flowering to prevent blossom drop and boost fruit size.
Use blue sticky traps for Thrips and yellow sticky traps for Whiteflies.

commonDiseases.name: Chilli Leaf Curl & Murda Disease
symptoms: Upward curling of leaves (Boat-shape) caused by Thrips
Downward curling of leaves caused by Mites
Crinkling, thickening, and brittle leaves with stunted growth
causes: Hot dry weather followed by humid spells fostering thrip/mite multiplication
organicTreatment: Spray 10,000 ppm Neem oil (Azadirachtin) @ 2 mL/L water
Apply Wettable Sulfur 80% WDG @ 3 g/L for mites
chemicalTreatment: Fipronil 5% SC @ 2 mL/L water for Thrips
Spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 1 mL/L water for Mites
prevention: Erect barrier crops like 4 rows of Sorghum around field
Maintain adequate soil moisture with drip irrigation
Dip seedling roots in Imidacloprid solution before transplanting

name: Wheat
soilType: Well-drained fertile clay loam or loam
growthTips: First irrigation at Crown Root Initiation (CRI stage, 21 days after sowing) is most crucial.
Avoid excess water at maturity to prevent lodging.
Ensure balanced N-P-K (120:60:40 kg/ha) with Zinc sulfate (25 kg/ha).

commonDiseases.name: Yellow / Stripe Rust
symptoms: Bright yellow stripe-like pustules arranged in linear rows on leaves
Yellow powdery spores on hands when rubbing leaves
Premature leaf drying leading to shriveled grain
causes: Cool temperatures (10-15°C) with continuous fog or dew in North India
organicTreatment: Spray Trichoderma viride @ 5g/L water at first sign
Dust sulfur powder @ 10 kg/acre in calm morning air
prevention: Plant rust-resistant varieties (HD-2967, HD-3086, DBW-187, DBW-222)

name: Maize (Corn)
soilType: Deep fertile loam with good organic matter and excellent drainage
growthTips: Critical irrigation stages are knee-high stage, tasseling, and silking stage.
Fall Armyworm monitoring must begin from 7 days after germination.

commonDiseases.name: Fall Armyworm (FAW)
symptoms: Pin-holes and window pane feeding on young leaves
Heavy ragged feeding in plant whorl filled with sawdust-like frass
Larvae with inverted Y mark on head
causes: Warm temperatures and continuous maize monoculture
organicTreatment: Application of sand/ash mixture (9:1) or neem cake powder into leaf whorls
Spray Metarhizium anisopliae @ 5g/L water into whorls
prevention: Synchronized community sowing in the region
Install FAW pheromone traps @ 5 per acre
